title: Continuity pocket brief - 2026-06-30
content:
Purpose:
A compact handoff note for the 06/30 UTC-midday rotation. Intentionally lightweight — pocket-sized checklist + quick context for the incoming engineer. Includes a short incident recap (P2 cache pressure this morning), immediate follow-ups, and a set of runbook draft changes to consider.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Morning spike at ~07:12 UTC: high tail latency on hosted API; brief increase in 95/99 latencies for text-generation routes. Root cause narrowed to router process memory growth leading to increased GC pauses on two serving nodes in us-central1.
- Traffic remained within SLA overall; automatic fallback to model-compact variants activated for ~8 minutes.
- No customer-facing errors (4xx/5xx), but sustained latency bump triggered alerts and on-call pager.
- Mitigation completed at 07:21 UTC by restarting affected router processes and enabling temporary request-throttling in the routing layer.

Status now:
- All nodes healthy, latency back to baseline; daily synthetic checks green.
- Temporary throttling disabled at 08:05 UTC after monitoring window.
- Post-incident partial mitigation: rolling restart of router process on a small cohort (3 nodes) scheduled midnight local for stability.

Action items (short):
1) Short-term (priority): finish quick analysis of GC traces attached to SRE-4821. Diego has the core dump and GC profiles. Expected time: 2–3 hours.
2) Mid-term: update router process memory-health check and add an explicit eviction threshold to avoid long GC pauses (ticket INFRA-913).
3) Long-term: consider introducing incremental shard rebalancing logic to reduce per-process state growth under skewed request patterns. Add to Q3 roadmap backlog.

Who owns what (right now):
- Incident lead: Aisha Patel (me) — initial triage, restart, and throttling policy toggle.
- Follow-up analysis: Diego Ramos — GC trace analysis and hypothesis write-up (see SRE-4821).
- Runbook edits: Marco Li — will draft runbook snippet for router memory thresholds and throttling knobs (PR linked).
- Monitoring: Samira O'Connell — tune alert thresholds for sustained 95th latency elevation.

Timeline (concise):
- 07:12 UTC: Pager received — latency notices for /v1/generate-text at 95/99p.
- 07:14–07:18 UTC: Quick triage, identified router node memory > 78% on two nodes (rtr-usc-03 & rtr-usc-08). Heap profiles captured.
- 07:19 UTC: Enabled temporary route-level throttling (20% reduction) to buy headroom.
- 07:21 UTC: Restarted router processes on affected nodes; observed GC cycles clearing memory.
- 07:30–07:55 UTC: Monitoring for regressions, no recurrence.
- 08:05 UTC: Disabled throttling; system stable.

Logs and evidence to review (short pointers):
- GC profiles: attached to JIRA SRE-4821 comments (Diego).
- Router logs: GH artifact logs/2026-06-30/router-usc-*.log (PR linked above).
- Metric dashboards: latency-per-route (console -> hosted-api -> per-route) and memory-usage heatmap for router fleet.

Customer impact notes:
- No direct error reports received from customers. Telemetry shows slightly slower responses for long-context requests during the 07:12–07:21 window.
- CS notified by on-call: short note sent to #cs-ops with summary and that no action required from customers.

Follow-ups to complete in the next 72 hours:
- [ ] Diego: post a short summary of GC analysis into SRE-4821 and recommend whether GC tuning or stickier routing is better.
- [ ] Marco: draft runbook snippet for router memory thresholds + command set for safe restart. Include exact kubectl commands and expected downtime.
- [ ] Samira: update alert rules to avoid noisy alarms for single-spike events; evaluate moving to sustained-window checks (3m -> 10m) for 95p latency.
- [ ] Ops: schedule rolling restart of router cohort (non-peak) and validate memory behavior.

Runbook draft notes (inlined — please copy into runbook editor and shape):
- Title: Router process memory spike — detection and mitigation (draft)
- Severity triggers: 95p latency > 2x baseline for > 3 minutes OR router process RSS > 70% of node allocatable for > 5 minutes.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Check console metrics: router-memory-usage, per-node heap, request-rate-by-route.
  2) If RSS > 75% on multiple nodes: enable routing throttle at 20% across model-heavy routes (CLI: infractl route throttle set --scope hosted-api --pct 20).
  3) If throttling insufficient in 3 minutes: restart router process on the highest-RSS node (kubectl rollout restart deployment/router --namespace serving --field-selector metadata.name=<node>).
  4) After restart: verify memory drops and check for traffic spillover. Roll back throttling when 95p under threshold for two consecutive 5m windows.
- Postmortem hooks: attach heapdumps and GC trace to JIRA, tag with INFRA-913 for follow-up.

Notes on alternatives considered (brief):
- We debated introducing a local eviction policy for router-side LRU cache; downside is potential quality regressions for repeated short-session users.
- GC tuning could reduce pause times but may increase memory usage; need data from Diego's traces to decide.

Open questions (please flag during handoff):
- Was any customer correlated with the traffic skew that triggered the memory growth? (Samira to query request-tags for heavy-senders.)
- Is the current router JVM image pinned to our GC tuning baseline? (Infra to confirm image tags)
- Do we want to run an A/B with compact-model fallback earlier as a safety valve?

Notes-to-self / scribbles (informal):
- Consider a small unit test that replays the morning traffic signature against router local caches — can do in staging with replay harness.
- Add a dashboard panel showing per-node GC pause-time percentiles (useful signal).

Hand-off checklist for incoming shift:
- [ ] Read this brief.
- [ ] Confirm SLOs on latency dashboard for hosted-api.
- [ ] Check SRE-4821 for Diego's GC traces.
- [ ] Confirm scheduled rolling restart time (Ops calendar).
- [ ] Keep an eye on model-compact fallback rates for next 24 hours.

If you need to escalate during your shift:
- Pager still active -> follow incident runbook and notify Lead on Slack @oncall-leads.
- If regeneration of router processes fails on >2 nodes, escalate to eng-platform rotation and create a SEV-3 incident.

Useful links (copy-paste):
- SRE ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-4821
- Infra follow-up: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFRA-913
- GH PR for initial mitigation scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1248
- Console dashboard (latency): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/hosted-api/latency-per-route

Signature: Aisha (on-call, eng-sre)

-- end of pocket brief --

Appendix (raw snippets / copyable commands):
- Check top memory nodes: kubectl top nodes --selector=role=router --no-headers | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 10
- Restart router deployment (example): kubectl rollout restart deployment/router -n serving --field-selector metadata.name=rtr-usc-03
- Toggle throttle (infractl): infractl route throttle set --scope hosted-api --pct 20 --reason "oncall mitigation 2026-06-30"
